chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, who said:

I entered upon 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام one day, and he said: “O Hakam, do you know the verse by which 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام used to know his killer, and by which he used to know the tremendous matters that he would relate to the people?” Al-Hakam said: So I said to myself, “I have come upon a knowledge from the knowledge of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn; by that I will know those tremendous matters.” He said: So I said, “No, by Allah, I do not know.” Then I said, “The verse—inform me of it, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.”
He said: “It is, by Allah, the saying of Allah, Mighty is His remembrance:”
“And We did not send before you any Messenger, nor Prophet, nor Muhaddath.”
And 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام was a Muhaddath.

Then a man called 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd—who was a maternal brother of 'Ali—said to him: “Glory be to Allah! A Muhaddath?” as though he was rejecting that. Then Abu Ja'far عليه السلام turned toward us and said: “Indeed, by Allah, the son of your mother had already known that.” He said: So when he said that, the man fell silent. Then he said: “It is that concerning which Abu al-Khattab was destroyed, for he did not understand the interpretation of the Muhaddath and the Prophet.”

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet, distinguished here from a مُحَدَّث
key_terms.الْآيَةَ: the verse being asked about as proof-text
key_terms.الْأُمُورَ الْعِظَامَ: the tremendous or grave matters he informed people about
key_terms.تَأْوِيلُ: the true meaning or proper interpretation
key_terms.قَاتِلَهُ: his killer, referring to foreknowledge of who would kill him
key_terms.مُحَدَّثًا: one who is spoken to or inspired, without being a Prophet
key_terms.هَلَكَ: was destroyed, meaning fell into ruin through doctrinal error

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by saying Imam 'Ali عليه السلام was مُحَدَّث and not a Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام as مُحَدَّث, one divinely addressed or inspired without being a Prophet, and links this to his knowledge of grave unseen matters. It also shows that misunderstanding the distinction between a مُحَدَّث and a Prophet leads to deviation, making the report significant for Shia discussions of the Imams’ special knowledge and rank.
